stanzas: Comme tu a chi tiene mente,
orig.credit: Giambattista De Curtis, the Neapolitan text as quoted on Italian Wikipedia

stanzas: See the sea, how beautiful it is,
as you do to whoever looks at you,
And you say: "I am leaving, goodbye!"
You go away from this heart…
Have you the heart not to come back?
Do not give me this torment!
what treasures it holds at its bottom:
whoever has travelled the whole world
has not seen it as it is here.
They would like to kiss you.
And you say: "I am leaving, goodbye!"
You go away from this heart
Have you the heart not to come back?
Do not give me this torment!

notes: Surriento is the Neapolitan name of Sorrento, on the Bay of Naples.
Lines 1.3-1.4: literally 'like you to whoever keeps you in mind (looks at you), / whom, awake, you make dream'.
Line 2.2: siente means both 'hear' and 'smell'; sciure arance, orange flowers.
Lines 3.4 and 7.4: tiene 'o core 'e nun turnà?, literally 'do you have the heart not to return?'.
Line 4.4: famme campà, literally 'make me live', 'let me live'.
Line 5.4: comm'a ccà, 'as here', i.e. the like of what is here.
Line 6.1: sirene, the sirens of myth.
